diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition line 31 permits arbitrary D,O subsets of Z^2. Remarks line 50 fixes D={0,1,2,3}x{0,1,2}, O={p,q}, p=(0,0), q=(1,0), a=(0,1), s=(2,1), and K={-1,0,1}^2, satisfying the stated finite K and positive stride requirements.

Formula line 34 gives a+s⊙p=(0,1) and a+s⊙q=(2,1). The circles are at those coordinates and the rightward arrow has displacement s⊙(q-p)=(2,0), exactly the coordinatewise multiplication specified on line 37.

The first anchor plus K is {-1,0,1}x{0,1,2}, nine sites. The blue square contains those nine lattice sites; six at x=0,1 lie in the drawn D boundary, and three red hollow sites at x=-1 lie outside D and have x-tilde=0 by the zero-padding definition on line 31.

Each six nonzero-capable sample is the original row vector in R^{C_in}; multiplication on the right by W_delta in R^{C_in x C_out} yields a row vector in R^{C_out}, as does b. The illustration uses anchor+delta, without reversing offsets, matching the cross-correlation convention on line 37. It adds no claim about invariance under the cropped boundary.
This is a definition with no proof; the definition and its formula remain untouched and fully specify the layer independently of the illustrative specialization.
